messages:
Ethan (sales): Quick help — BridgeTech POC needs the vendor security questionnaire answered + a PO. Procurement attached an escrow requirement and a tax withholding line they want in the PO. Can legal + finance review? SQ: https://sq.company.com/BridgeTech-POC

Priya (legal): Assigning. Can you paste the exact escrow language they provided? If it's a third-party escrow we'll need the escrow agent details and jurisdiction. Also: are they asking to change the MSA or add an appendix to the order form?

Miguel (solutions): For the POC we're planning to bill via order form: estimated spend ~ $18k over 30 days (mix of credits + invoice). No dedicated infra. Sam — did procurement attach their standard PO template?

Sam (AE): Yes — attached PO (PO# BT-2234). Procurement insists on: (1) escrow for source, (2) an indemnity carveout for their subcontractors, (3) Net45 payment term.

Tara (finance): For POCs under $25k we prefer Net30. Net45 will need manager approval. Also escrow complicates onboarding — need to know payment method (wire vs ACH). If they insist on escrow agent holding source, legal + procurement must sign off.

Ethan (sales): Copy. Priya, we'll paste their escrow wording below so you can propose a redline.

Priya (legal): Their original: "Supplier shall deposit source code with Escrow Agent; release upon insolvency or breach; agent jurisdiction: EU." Not acceptable as-is. Proposed redline (keeps scope narrow):

```
Escrow Agent: The parties may agree to deposit Customer-deliverables limited to compiled binaries and documentation. Source code escrow is only permitted with prior written approval from Redwood legal and subject to an escrow agreement executed by the parties and the escrow agent. Redwood's liability for escrow release is limited as set forth in the MSA.
```

Also push back on the broad tax withholding language. Proposed replacement: `Customer shall comply with applicable tax withholding laws; any withholding amounts may be credited against fees only where Redwood is the withholding agent.`

Miguel (solutions): That looks good. From an engineering perspective: do not include internal CI/build scripts or private keys. We can provide compiled artifacts and runbooks if escrow is approved.

Priya (legal): Affirmed — no CI scripts, no internal secrets. Escrow artifacts should be limited to distributable binaries, install/run notes, and contact info for the escrow agent. If they require more, escalate to legal leadership.

Sam (AE): On signature routing: BridgeTech procurement requests DocuSign with two signers (their PO signer + our finance). They also mentioned a preference for parallel signing to speed up. Can Redwood do parallel review + signing?

Tara (finance): We can sign via DocuSign once legal signs off. If they want parallel signing, we can configure signing order: Legal -> Finance -> Exec (if over threshold). For ~$18k PO, Legal + Finance signing order is fine. If procurement insists on Net45, I'll submit for manager approval but call out the risk.

DocuSign Bot: Created envelope 1830012370 for BridgeTech-PO. Status: waiting for Priya (legal) to sign. Link: https://docusign.com/envelopes/1830012370

Ethan (sales): Thanks everyone — I'll send the redline back to the buyer with our escrow language, confirm payment method (ACH vs wire) and ask if they can accept Net30. Looping in their procurement contact (Karim) on the message.

Priya (legal): If they accept Net30 and agree to the narrowed escrow scope, legal is comfortable. If they push for source release or a broad indemnity, escalate and do not sign until reviewed by me and counsel.

Tara (finance): Noted. Keep me posted on the payment method and final PO. I'll prep the DocuSign flow once legal signs. :thumbsup:

Sam (AE): I'll attach the buyer PO and the BridgeTech risk questionnaire responses in the thread after Ethan sends redline.

Ethan (sales): Will do. Thanks all.
